Fox National Aeronautics and Space Administration Glenn Research Center Cleveland, Ohio 44135 Abstract Ceramic thermal and environmental barrier coatings (TEBCs) are used in gas turbine engines to protect engine hot-section components in the harsh combustion environments, and extend component lifetimes
Combustor exit temperatures during the supersonic cruise will lead to turbine inlet temperatures around 167 °C (300 °F) higher than the current state-of-the-art for subsonic engines

NASA/TM—2008-215040 1 To take full advantage of the TEBC capability potential, an aggressive design approach—allowing greater temperature reductions through the coating systems and less cooling air to the components—is required whenever possible

As shown in figure 1, the development of revolutionary ceramic coatings, combined with improved single crystal Ni-base superalloy and CMC substrates, will result in a step increase in gas turbine engine blade, vane and combustor component temperature capability

Figure 2 is a schematic diagram showing how advanced ceramic barrier coatings with lower thermal conductivity and better temperature stability will allow the use of thinner coatings to achieve a larger temperature reduction in the higher operating temperature engines
